reader.requirement: At --std 85 a format 1 REPLACE whose pseudo-text-1 consists entirely of a separator comma or a separator semicolon (alone or several, with spaces) must be refused, while a pseudo-text-1 with a comma or semicolon beside another text word is legal; the witness covers ==,== only.
reader.edition-search: The check is MatchWords.Count == 0 in ScreenOperandPair's Whole arm, MatchWords dropping TextWordKind.SeparatorCommaOrSemicolon and DirectiveLine; grepped CopyProcessor.cs and TextWord.cs for Edition|CobolVersion|Year|Dialect|ConstructRegistry|EditionInfo: OperandScreen carries an edition but Content() never reads it, so the SR7 check is edition-blind, the same arm at 85 and 2023 (same rule in both).

reader.notes: The 1985 text bars 'a separator comma or a separator semicolon'; the compiler reads 'entirely' as any run of them, which is the only reading under which GR6b's matching (each is a single space) can find a match, so refusing == , ; == is not over-rejection. The message cites §2023:7.2.4.3 SR3 at --std 85, not §1985:XII.3.3 SR7.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-073/: q7commasemi.cob ==,;== (a comma followed by a semicolon is no separator, so ',;' is one item-3 text word) compiles and prints '[OK  ]'; q8debugcomma.cob, pseudo-text-1 holding only a debugging line with a separator comma, is refused COBOL2572 'pseudo-text-1 holds no text-word to match'; q9semieol.cob, a semicolon then a comma on the next line, is refused the same way. Each matches 'Pseudo-text-1 must not consist entirely of a separator comma or a separator semicolon' (OK §1985:XII.3.3 SR7) read with the Text Word definition (OK §1985:III.2 'Any other sequence of contiguous COBOL characters except comment lines and the word 'COPY', bounded by separators'). The '>>' defect of the SR3 case reaches SR7's count too, but no SR7 form (comma/semicolon only) is affected by it. Message cites §2023, quality only.
